text:
124 Hispanic students enrolled at Julian O. Strong Middle School in 2024-25
Julian O. Strong Middle School had 124 Hispanic students enrolled in the 2024-25 school year, a 9.5% decline from the previous year, according to the Michigan Department of Education.
Data show the school enrolled 651 students in the 2024-25 school year. Hispanic students made up 19% of the student body, the second-most represented ethnicity. White students were the largest group, accounting for 71% (462) of the student body.
The school is located in Melvindale-North Allen Park Schools District with a central office in Melvindale.
Among the four schools in Melvindale-North Allen Park Schools District, Melvindale High School recorded the highest enrollment of Hispanic students in the 2024-25 school year.
Academic performance in Michigan remains below pre-pandemic levels. The 2024 NAEP results show the share of students reaching the basic benchmark in core subjects is about 10 percentage points lower than in 2019, except for fourth-grade math, which declined by 2 points.
Achievement gaps between ethnic groups also persist. On average, Hispanic students scored 15 points below white students, while Black students scored about 30 points lower than their white peers.
